hooks.name: onTick

hooks.name: onCanRx
hooks.description: Função que o script define e a ECU chama para cada quadro CAN que passou por um filtro aberto com canRxAdd/canRxAddMask sem callback próprio. O vetor data tem dlc bytes (1-based).

params.name: data
params.description: Bytes do quadro, data[1] é o primeiro.

hooks.example:
canRxAdd(0x201)
function onCanRx(bus, id, dlc, data)
  if id == 0x201 then rpmFromCan = (data[1] * 256 + data[2]) / 4 end
end

settings.name: clFuelCommon.exhaustVolumeToSensor
settings.description: Exhaust volume between the exhaust valve and the O2/lambda sensor. Feeds the physical model used to derive closed loop correction speed (both short and long term) and to avoid learning on lambda feedback that still reflects the previous operating point. Default covers most small NA/turbo manifolds - only change if you know how to measure it. Geometry data also read by the calibration assistants. This is one single parameter, shown both in the closed loop general settings and in Engine Geometry: editing it in one place changes the other. To estimate from the pipe: volume (mL) = pi/4 x inner diameter (mm)^2 x length (mm) / 1000, adding the manifold runners and collector.

settings.name: clFuelCommon.minClt

settings.name: clFuelCommon.minLambda
settings.description: Below this lambda value fuel corrections are paused. Prevents the ECU from correcting during intentionally rich conditions such as acceleration enrichment or cold start. Typical value is 0.82 which corresponds to a moderately rich mixture.

settings.name: clFuelCommon.noFuelTrimAfterAccelTime
settings.description: Pause closed loop fueling for this long AFTER the acceleration or deceleration enrichment has ended (the exponential tail included). settings.name: enableEvoNet
settings.description: evoNet: let displays (WideLink, evoDash) discover this ECU's channels by themselves over CAN, instead of relying on a layout hardcoded in the display firmware. Adds ~2 CAN frames per second (identity + availability) on bus 1 using extended IDs 0x1E0000xx, plus replies to catalog requests. Off by default: a display that does not speak evoNet is unaffected, and the classic Evotech CAN broadcast above keeps working either way.

settings.name: enableEvoNetHighRiskActions
settings.description: Allow a display to request HIGH RISK evoNet actions: engine start/stop and valet mode. Off by default and independent of the evoNet switch above -- turning on channel discovery must never, by itself, expose engine start to the bus. Even with this on, the ECU still checks its own preconditions (engine stopped, no active cut, vehicle stopped) and requires a challenge-response exchange; this bit only decides whether it will consider the request at all.

Independent from, and normally higher than, the common closed-loop minimum temperature above - learning writes to persistent memory, so it's worth being more conservative about when to start than simply applying trims already learned.

settings.name: ltitIgnitionOffSaveDelay

settings.name: ltitIgnitionOnDelay

settings.name: luaCanRxWorkaround
settings.description: global_can_data performance hack

settings.name: mafFilterParameter
settings.description: Legacy MAF sensor smoothing: larger value = more smoothing (time constant = value / RPM seconds). Applied to the sensor signal itself and runs before the manifold fill model below. Keep at 1 (off) when the manifold fill model is used to avoid filtering twice.

settings.name: mafManifoldEtaV
settings.description: Volumetric efficiency used only to compute the manifold time constant (not the fuel VE table). 0.85 is typical for a naturally aspirated engine. Lower values make the lag longer.

settings.name: mafManifoldLeadMs
settings.description: Optional anticipation of the air estimate to compensate the time between the fuel calculation and the intake event. Moves the estimate a bounded fraction of the way towards the MAF reading - never beyond it. 0 = off.

settings.name: mafManifoldTauMaxMs
settings.description: Upper limit of the manifold time constant. Protects very low RPM (cranking and stall) where the physical value would reach seconds.

settings.name: mafManifoldTauScale
settings.description: Fine adjustment multiplying the computed manifold time constant. 1.00 keeps the physical value. Use above 1 if logs show the cylinder air still lags the MAF more than modeled - below 1 if it overshoots.

settings.name: mafManifoldVolumeL
settings.description: Effective intake volume between the MAF/throttle and the intake valves. The MAF measures the air entering this volume, while the cylinders only receive the air that has filled it: during a throttle step they differ for a short time. The air used for fuel and load follows the MAF through a first-order lag with time constant 120 x volume / (VE reference x displacement x RPM). 0 turns the model off (air equals the MAF reading). Use the plenum plus runners volume if known. A larger volume means a slower - longer lag. This is one single parameter, shown both in the MAF settings and in Engine Geometry: editing it in one place changes the other.

settings.name: map.sensor.highValue
settings.description: kPa/psi value at high volts

settings.name: map.sensor.lowValue
settings.description: kPa/psi value at low volts

settings.name: mapCamDetectionAnglePosition
settings.description: Magic engine phase: we compare instant MAP at X to instant MAP at x+360 angle in one complete cycle

settings.name: mapErrorDetectionTooHigh
settings.description: kPa/psi value which is too high to be true

settings.name: mapErrorDetectionTooLow
settings.description: kPa/psi value which is too low to be true

settings.name: mapExpAverageAlpha
settings.description: A higher alpha (closer to 1) means the EMA reacts more quickly to changes in the data. '1' means no filtering, 0.98 would be some filtering.

settings.name: mapHighValueVoltage
settings.description: MAP voltage for low point

settings.name: mapLowValueVoltage
settings.description: MAP voltage for low point

settings.name: mapMinBufferLength
settings.description: This many MAP samples are used to estimate the current MAP. This many samples are considered, and the minimum taken. Recommended value is 1 for single-throttle engines, and your number of cylinders for individual throttle bodies.

settings.name: mapSyncThreshold
settings.description: Delta kPa/psi for MAP sync

settings.name: maxAcClt
settings.description: Above this CLT, disable AC to prevent overheating the engine. Set to 0 to disable check.

settings.name: maxAcPressure
settings.description: value of A/C pressure in kPa/psi after that compressor is disengaged

settings.name: maxAcRpm
settings.description: Above this RPM, disable AC. Set to 0 to disable check.

settings.name: maxAcTps
settings.description: Above this TPS, disable AC. Set to 0 to disable check.

settings.name: maxCamPhaseResolveRpm
settings.description: Below this RPM, use camshaft information to synchronize the crank's position for full sequential operation. Use this if your cam sensor does weird things at high RPM. Set to 0 to disable, and always use cam to help sync crank.

settings.name: maxDwellMs
settings.description: Maximum coil dwell (charge time) allowed for any single spark pulse, applied after all dwell corrections -- including cranking's fixed dwell value and multispark. 0 disables this software limit (today's behavior, unaffected). This is a configuration envelope, not a safe-for-any-coil default -- set it from your coil/driver's actual maximum charge time. Does not change the MC33810 hardware dwell timer, which remains a separate, independent protection.

settings.name: maxIdleVss
settings.description: Above this speed, disable closed loop idle control. Set to 0 to disable (allow closed loop idle at any speed).

settings.name: maximumIgnitionTiming
settings.description: Maximum timing advance allowed. No spark on any cylinder will ever fire before this angle BTDC. For example, setting 45 here means no spark ever fires earlier than 45 deg BTDC

settings.name: maxInjectorDutyInstant
settings.description: This sets an immediate limit on injector duty cycle. If this threshold is reached, the system will immediately cut the injectors.

settings.name: maxInjectorDutySustained
settings.description: This limit allows injectors to operate up to the specified duty cycle percentage for a short period (as defined by the delay). After this delay, if the duty cycle remains above the limit, it will trigger a cut.

settings.name: maxInjectorDutySustainedTimeout
settings.description: Timeout period for duty cycle over the sustained limit to trigger duty cycle protection.

settings.name: maxInstantRetardStepDeg
settings.description: Maximum single-cycle retard step for the clutch guard feedforward. Beyond this, the remainder becomes spark cut (thermally safer at high MAP than a large instant retard step).

settings.name: maxOilPressureTimeout
settings.description: Delay before cutting fuel due to extra high oil pressure. Use this to ignore short pressure blips and sensor noise.

settings.name: maxTorqueRateNmPerSec
settings.description: Hard ceiling on rate of change of smoothed torque -- worst-case backstop, not the primary shaping mechanism (that is torqueSmoothingTauSec). Rarely engaged in practice.

settings.name: mc33810DisableRecoveryMode
settings.description: See Over/Undervoltage Shutdown/Retry bit in documentation

settings.name: mc33810Maxi
settings.description: Maximum coil charge current, 1A step

settings.name: mc33810Nomi
settings.description: Nominal coil charge current, 0.25A step

settings.name: mc33_hpfp_i_hold_off
settings.description: How long to deactivate power when hold current is reached before applying power again

settings.name: mc33_hpfp_max_hold
settings.description: Maximum amount of time the solenoid can be active before assuming a programming error

settings.name: mc33_hvolt
settings.description: Boost Voltage

settings.name: mc33_i_boost
settings.description: Boost Current

settings.description: Hold Current

settings.name: mc33_i_peak
settings.description: Peak Current

settings.name: mc33_t_hold_tot
settings.description: Hold phase duration

settings.name: mc33_t_max_boost
settings.description: Maximum allowed boost phase time. If the injector current doesn't reach the threshold before this time elapses, it is assumed that the injector is missing or has failed open circuit.

settings.name: mc33_t_min_boost
settings.description: Minimum allowed time for the boost phase. If the boost target current is reached before this time elapses, it is assumed that the injector has failed short circuit.

settings.name: mc33_t_peak_tot
settings.description: Peak phase duration

settings.name: measureMapOnlyInOneCylinder
settings.description: Useful for individual intakes

settings.name: minAcPressure
settings.description: value of A/C pressure in kPa/psi before that compressor is disengaged

settings.name: minimumBoostClosedLoopMap
settings.description: Minimum MAP before closed loop boost is enabled. Use to prevent misbehavior upon entering boost.

settings.name: minimumIgnitionTiming
settings.description: Minimum timing advance allowed. No spark on any cylinder will ever fire after this angle BTDC. For example, setting -10 here means no spark ever fires later than 10 deg ATDC. Note that this only concerns the primary spark: any trailing sparks or multispark may violate this constraint.

settings.name: minimumOilPressureTimeout
settings.description: Delay before cutting fuel due to low oil pressure. Use this to ignore short pressure blips and sensor noise.

settings.name: minOilPressureAfterStart
settings.description: Expected oil pressure after starting the engine. If oil pressure does not reach this level within 5 seconds of engine start, fuel will be cut. Set to 0 to disable and always allow starting.

settings.name: multisparkDwell
settings.description: This sets the dwell time for subsequent sparks. The main spark's dwell is set by the dwell table.

settings.name: multisparkMaxExtraSparkCount
settings.description: Configures the maximum number of extra sparks to fire (does not include main spark)

settings.name: multisparkMaxRpm
settings.description: Disable multispark above this engine speed.

settings.name: multisparkMaxSparkingAngle
settings.description: This parameter sets the latest that the last multispark can occur after the main ignition event. For example, if the ignition timing is 30 degrees BTDC, and this parameter is set to 45, no multispark will ever be fired after 15 degrees ATDC.

settings.name: multisparkSparkDuration
settings.description: How long to wait for the spark to fire before recharging the coil for another spark.

settings.name: nitrousIgnitionRetard
settings.description: Retard timing to remove from actual final timing (after all corrections) due to additional air.

settings.name: oilTemperatureCritical
settings.description: Critical oil temperature. 0 disables this rule.

settings.name: oilTemperatureHysteresis
settings.description: Oil-temperature recovery hysteresis.

settings.name: oilTemperatureTimeoutMs
settings.description: Oil-temperature critical persistence.

settings.name: oilTempSensor.config.bias_resistor
settings.description: Pull-up resistor value on your board

settings.name: oilTempSensor.config.tempC_1
settings.description: these values are in Celcius

settings.name: oilTempSharedMode
settings.description: Oil temperature sensor mode. Off: independent sensor read through the on-board pull-up using the 3-point resistance calibration. On: sensor shared with another ECU, converted from pin voltage using the voltage curve.

settings.name: pauseEtbControl
settings.description: Disable the electronic throttle motor and DC idle motor for testing. This mode is for testing ETB/DC idle position sensors, etc without actually driving the throttle.

settings.name: pfiFuelPressureMaximum
settings.description: Critical maximum PFI injector differential pressure. 0 disables the high-pressure side.

settings.name: pfiFuelPressureMinimum
settings.description: Critical minimum PFI injector differential pressure. 0 disables the low-pressure side.

settings.name: pfiFuelPressureTimeoutMs
settings.description: Continuous out-of-range time before a PFI-pressure fuel cut. 0 requires a currently bad valid sample.

settings.name: pidExtraForLowRpm
settings.description: Increases PID reaction for RPM<target by adding extra percent to PID-error

settings.name: ppsExpAverageAlpha
settings.description: A higher alpha (closer to 1) means the EMA reacts more quickly to changes in the data. '100%' means no filtering, 98% would be some filtering.

settings.name: ppsSecondaryMaximum
settings.description: For Toyota ETCS-i, use ~69%

settings.name: primingDelay
settings.description: Delay to allow fuel pressure to build before firing the priming pulse.

settings.name: rpmHardLimit
settings.description: set rpm_hard_limit X

settings.name: rpmHardLimitHyst
settings.description: Sets a buffer below the RPM hard limit, helping avoid rapid cycling of cut actions by defining a range within which RPM must drop before cut actions are re-enabled. Hysterisis: if the hard limit is 7200rpm and rpmHardLimitHyst is 200rpm, then when the ECU sees 7200rpm, fuel/ign will cut, and stay cut until 7000rpm (7200-200) is reached

settings.name: rpmSoftLimitFuelAdded
settings.description: % of fuel ADDED during window

settings.name: rpmSoftLimitTimingRetard
settings.description: Degrees of timing REMOVED from actual timing during soft RPM limit window

settings.name: rpmSoftLimitWindowSize
settings.description: Window that the correction will be added throughout (example, if rpm limit is 7000, and rpmSoftLimitWindowSize is 200, the corrections activate at 6800RPM, creating a 200rpm window)

settings.name: rusefiVerbose29b
settings.description: Use 11 bit (standard) or 29 bit (extended) IDs for rusEFI verbose CAN format.

settings.name: sanderoPumpSpeed
settings.description: Sandero pump speed control value

settings.name: sdCardLogFrequency
settings.description: Rate the ECU will log to the SD card, in hz (log lines per second).

settings.name: sdTriggerLog
settings.description: 'Trigger' mode will write a high speed log of trigger events (warning: uses lots of space!). 'Normal' mode will write a standard MLG of sensors, engine function, etc. similar to the one captured in TunerStudio.

settings.name: secondaryInjectorFuelReferencePressure
settings.description: This is the pressure at which your injector flow is known. For example if your injectors flow 400cc/min at 3.5 bar, enter 350kpa here.

settings.name: silentTriggerError
settings.description: Sometimes we have a performance issue while printing error

settings.name: skippedWheelOnCam
settings.description: Where is your primary skipped wheel located?

settings.name: smoothingClutchGuardEnabled
settings.description: Enable the clutch-release overspeed guard (Mechanism B).

settings.name: smoothingClutchMinTps
settings.description: Minimum TPS at the clutch-release instant (or, in RPM x TPS mode, minimum sustained TPS) for the guard to arm.

settings.name: smoothingClutchWindowMs
settings.description: Time window after a clutch-release event during which the guard stays armed.

settings.name: sparkHardwareLatencyCorrection
settings.description: Compensates for trigger delay due to belt stretch, or other electromechanical issues. beware that raising this value advances ignition timing!

settings.name: speedometerPulsePerKm
settings.description: Number of speedometer pulses per kilometer travelled.

settings.name: startCrankingDuration
settings.description: Maximum time to crank starter when start/stop button is pressed

settings.name: startUpFuelPumpDuration
settings.description: on IGN voltage detection turn fuel pump on to build fuel pressure

settings.name: stepperDcInvertedPins
settings.description: Enable if DC-motor driver (H-bridge) inverts the signals (eg. RZ7899 on Hellen boards)

settings.name: stepperMaxDutyCycle
settings.description: Use to limit the max.current through the stepper motor (100% = no limit)

settings.name: stepperMinDutyCycle
settings.description: Use to limit the current when the stepper motor is idle, not moving (100% = no limit)

settings.name: stft.deadband
settings.description: Minimum AFR error required to trigger a correction. If the current error is smaller than this value, no correction is applied. Prevents oscillation when the mixture is already close to the target.

settings.name: stft.maxAdd
settings.description: Maximum percentage the short-term trim can add to the base fuel. Keep this value reasonable (3-5%) to avoid masking underlying tune problems.

settings.name: stft.maxRemove
settings.description: Maximum percentage the short-term trim can remove from the base fuel. Keep this value reasonable (3-5%) to avoid masking underlying tune problems.

settings.name: stft.tauBase
settings.description: Minimum reference time constant for LTFT learning only. The exhaust delay model may increase this reference, then the LTFT slowdown factor is applied. Default 5 seconds. Increasing it slows LTFT learning. This field does not adjust STFT speed: STFT always uses PI with gains derived from the modeled delay.

settings.name: stoichRatioPrimary
settings.description: Stoichiometric ratio for your primary fuel. When Flex Fuel is enabled, this value is used when the Flex Fuel sensor indicates E0. E0 = 14.7 E10 = 14.1 E85 = 9.9 E100 = 9.0

settings.name: stoichRatioSecondary
settings.description: Stoichiometric ratio for your secondary fuel. This value is used when the Flex Fuel sensor indicates E100, typically 9.0

settings.name: tachPulseDuractionMs
settings.description: Duration in ms or duty cycle depending on selected mode

settings.name: tachPulseDurationAsDutyCycle
settings.description: Treat milliseconds value as duty cycle value, i.e. 0.5ms would become 50%

settings.name: tcClutchSettleTimeMs
settings.description: Time after clutch release before TC re-arms. Avoids reading driveline shock right after clutch engagement as wheel slip.

settings.name: tcCutRampRatePctPerSec
settings.description: Maximum rate of change of applied spark cut. Limits how fast torque is removed/returned, avoids a driveline jolt.

settings.name: tcEnabled
settings.description: Enable Traction Control estimation and ignition retard / spark cut. Curves are zero by default. Disabled and clutch-open states neutralize both outputs.

settings.name: tcFilterTimeConstantMs
settings.description: Time constant of the signed RPM acceleration filter in Traction Wheel mode. Negative acceleration remains in the filter, only the resulting demand is clamped to zero. Higher = smoother but slower to react. 10 = nearly unfiltered, 100 = default, 1000 = very smooth.

settings.name: tChargeAirCoefMax
settings.description: Heat transfer coefficient at high flow, as defined by "max air flow". 0 means the air charge is fully heated to the same temperature as CLT. 1 means the air charge gains no heat, and enters the cylinder at the temperature measured by IAT.

settings.name: tChargeAirCoefMin
settings.description: Heat transfer coefficient at zero flow. 0 means the air charge is fully heated to the same temperature as CLT. 1 means the air charge gains no heat, and enters the cylinder at the temperature measured by IAT.

settings.name: tChargeAirDecrLimit
settings.description: Maximum allowed rate of decrease allowed for the estimated charge temperature

settings.name: tChargeAirFlowMax
settings.description: High flow point for heat transfer estimation. Set this to perhaps 50-75% of your maximum airflow at wide open throttle.

settings.name: tChargeAirIncrLimit
settings.description: Maximum allowed rate of increase allowed for the estimated charge temperature

settings.name: tcMinMap
settings.description: Minimum MAP for TC to arm. 0 = MAP does not gate TC.

settings.name: tcMinTps
settings.description: Minimum driver pedal/throttle position (PPS/TPS) for TC to arm.

settings.name: tcRetardRampRateDegPerSec
settings.description: Maximum rate of change of applied ignition retard. Limits how fast torque is removed/returned, avoids a driveline jolt.

settings.name: thermalProtectionTemp
settings.description: Critical CLT temperature — all fans forced ON above this threshold

settings.name: throttlePedalSecondaryWOTVoltage
settings.description: Pedal in the floor

settings.name: throttlePedalWOTVoltage
settings.description: Pedal in the floor

settings.name: torqueAddEnabled
settings.description: Enable advance-ceiling torque add (Mechanism C). Only engages transiently while the smoothing ramp needs more torque than the map gives at the current load, and only when current load is below the load where the row's advance peak occurs (no knock-margin risk). Disabled by default -- torque gain from this mechanism is not quantified.

settings.name: torqueReductionActivationTemperature
settings.description: Minimum coolant temperature for the shift cut to arm. 0 = no limit

settings.name: torqueReductionArmingApp
settings.description: Minimum driver pedal/throttle position (PPS/TPS), in %, for the shift cut to arm. Below this value the cut never acts, on upshifts or downshifts

settings.name: torqueReductionArmingRpm
settings.description: Minimum RPM for the shift cut to arm. If the button or clutch is shared with Launch Control and there is no working speed sensor, below this RPM the input launches and above it cuts the shift. With a working speed sensor the speed decides instead

settings.name: torqueReductionEnabled
settings.description: Enable the shift cut (flat shift): while the trigger is active it cuts ignition and sets an absolute ignition timing, on upshifts and downshifts

settings.name: torqueSmoothingDeadbandNm
settings.description: Retard deadband: the first N Nm of gap between smoothed and target torque produce zero retard, symmetric for both directions. smoothedNm itself keeps ramping normally (real lag is preserved for genuinely sustained transitions) -- only the retard calculation ignores the first N Nm of that lag. Tuned to absorb estimatedTorqueNm sensor noise and light tip-in/gear-shift recovery without masking real cut-off/WOT or clutch-flare events. Validated by simulation against tuning_logs/mao1452.

settings.name: torqueSmoothingEnabled
settings.description: Master enable for ignition-based torque smoothing. When disabled: DFCO fuel cut begins immediately (pre-existing behavior, no ignition-ramp wait) and no smoothing/torque-add is applied anywhere. See docs/design/torque-model-arbitration.md.

settings.name: torqueSmoothingTauSec
settings.description: Time constant of the torque-smoothing exponential filter (Mechanism A). Primary shaping parameter -- smaller = more responsive, larger = smoother. Default validated against real logged transitions.

settings.name: tpsAccelEnrichmentThreshold
settings.description: Maximum change delta of TPS percentage over the 'length'. Actual TPS change has to be above this value in order for TPS/TPS acceleration to kick in.

settings.name: tpsAccelFastAlpha
settings.description: Fast EMA alpha for TPS filtering (weight of the current sample). Higher = more responsive, more sensitive to sensor noise.

settings.name: tpsAccelFractionDivisor
settings.description: A fraction divisor: 1 or less = entire portion at once, or split into diminishing fractions

settings.name: tpsAccelFractionPeriod
settings.description: A delay in cycles between fuel-enrich. portions

settings.name: tpsAccelLookback
settings.description: Decay time for acceleration enrichment after a small tip-in (TPS barely moves). Does not affect detection, only how long the extra fuel lingers after the transient ends -- it fully tapers off over about 5x this value. Larger tip-ins scale toward the Accel - Full Tip-in setting below instead.

settings.name: tpsAccelLookbackMax
settings.description: Decay time for acceleration enrichment after the largest tip-ins (TPS sweeping through its full 0-100% range). Raise this if hard tip-ins still feel lean or hesitant right after the initial fuel pulse ends. Small tip-ins still use the Accel - Small Tip-in setting above.

settings.name: tpsAccelMaxEnrich
settings.description: Ceiling of the positive (acceleration) enrichment of the TPS/TPS table after the curves, in the unit of the enrichment mode: ms per cycle in Fixed pulse, fraction of the base fuel in Proportional (0.50 = +50%). 0 means no ceiling (factory default), only the fixed limits of the mode apply. The deceleration (lean) part is not limited by this ceiling.

settings.name: tpsAccelMinRate
settings.description: Minimum rate of throttle movement, in real percent per second (TPS % change divided by time), required to trigger acceleration enrichment. Before issue 35 the value was 10 times smaller than the real rate (it was mislabelled). Saved tunes are converted once at load (value x10). If set too low the enrichment fires on sensor noise or small throttle variations at steady speed causing unnecessary fuel spikes. If set too high fast tip-ins go undetected and the engine may stumble under hard acceleration. Typical starting point is 50 percent per second (factory default). Raise it if false enrichment occurs at cruise. Lower it if stumble persists on quick throttle openings.

settings.name: tpsAccelSlowAlpha
settings.description: Slow EMA alpha for TPS filtering (weight of the current sample). Lower = more inertia, used as the trailing reference the fast EMA is compared against.

settings.name: tpsAccelThreshold
settings.description: Fast-EMA minus slow-EMA divergence (in TPS %) required to keep an acceleration transient active. Also gates when the transient is considered over.

settings.name: tpsDecelEnleanmentMultiplier
settings.description: Unused -- superseded by the shared TPS/TPS accel table (see tpsTpsAccelTable) which now also drives decel enleanment with a sign flip. Kept only for config-layout/burn compatibility with older tunes.

settings.name: tpsDecelEnleanmentThreshold
settings.description: Unused -- superseded by the shared TPS/TPS accel table (see tpsTpsAccelTable) which now also drives decel enleanment with a sign flip. Kept only for config-layout/burn compatibility with older tunes.

settings.name: tpsDecelLookback
settings.description: Decay time for deceleration enleanment after a small throttle lift (TPS barely moves). Does not affect detection, only how long the correction lingers after the transient ends -- it fully tapers off over about 5x this value. Larger lifts scale toward the Decel - Full Lift setting below instead.

settings.name: tpsDecelLookbackMax
settings.description: Decay time for deceleration enleanment after the largest throttle lifts (TPS sweeping through its full 0-100% range). Small lifts still use the Decel - Small Lift setting above.

settings.name: tpsDecelThreshold
settings.description: Slow-EMA minus fast-EMA divergence (in TPS %) required to keep a deceleration transient active. Also gates when the transient is considered over.

settings.name: tpsDecelUsesCltRpmMult
settings.description: Whether the deceleration (lean) part of the acceleration enrichment is also multiplied by the RPM and coolant curves of the enrichment. Not scaled (factory default): only the enrichment of the acceleration part is scaled by CLT and RPM; the decel is the table value. Scaled: the former behavior, kept for tunes saved before issue 36. The flex fuel multiplier always applies to both.

settings.name: tpsErrorDetectionTooHigh
settings.description: TPS error detection: what throttle % is unrealistically high? Also used for accelerator pedal error detection if so equipped.

settings.name: tpsErrorDetectionTooLow
settings.description: TPS error detection: what throttle % is unrealistically low? Also used for accelerator pedal error detection if so equipped.

settings.name: tpsRateUnitCorrected
settings.description: Internal marker, not shown in the UI. Set when the TPS rate threshold and the TPS rate curve axis of this tune are in real percent per second (issue 35). A tune saved before that change reads Legacy and is converted once at load (threshold and axis x10), then marked. Do not edit.

settings.name: tpsSecondaryMaximum
settings.description: For Ford TPS, use 53%. For Toyota ETCS-i, use ~65%

settings.name: triggerCompCenterVolt
settings.description: Trigger comparator center point voltage

settings.name: triggerCompHystMax
settings.description: Trigger comparator hysteresis voltage (Max)

settings.name: triggerCompHystMin
settings.description: Trigger comparator hysteresis voltage (Min)

settings.name: triggerCompSensorSatRpm
settings.description: VR-sensor saturation RPM

settings.name: tunerStudioSerialSpeed
settings.description: Secondary TTL channel baud rate

settings.name: twoWireBatchIgnition
settings.description: This is needed if your coils are individually wired (COP) and you wish to use batch ignition (Wasted Spark).

settings.name: uartConsoleSerialSpeed
settings.description: Band rate for primary TTL

settings.name: useAdvanceCorrectionsForCranking
settings.description: This enables the various ignition corrections during cranking (IAT, CLT and PID idle). You probably don't need this.

settings.name: useCicPidForIdle
settings.description: Switch between Industrial and Cic PID implementation

settings.name: useCltBasedRpmLimit
settings.description: If enabled, use a curve for RPM limit (based on coolant temperature) instead of a constant value.

settings.name: useFixedBaroCorrFromMap
settings.description: Read MAP sensor on ECU start-up to use as baro value.

settings.name: useFordRedundantPps
settings.description: On some Ford and Toyota vehicles one of the pedal sensors is not linear on the full range, i.e. in the specific range of the positions we effectively have only one sensor.

settings.name: useFordRedundantTps
settings.description: On some Ford and Toyota vehicles one of the throttle sensors is not linear on the full range, i.e. in the specific range of the positions we effectively have only one sensor.

settings.name: useHbridgesToDriveIdleStepper
settings.description: If enabled we use two H-bridges to drive stepper idle air valve

settings.name: useIacPidMultTable
settings.description: This flag allows to use a special 'PID Multiplier' table (0.0-1.0) to compensate for nonlinear nature of IAC-RPM controller

settings.name: useIacTableForCoasting
settings.description: Override the IAC position during overrun and running conditions to help reduce engine breaking, this can be helpful for large engines in light weight cars or engines that have trouble returning to idle.

settings.name: useRawOutputToDriveIdleStepper
settings.description: If enabled we use four Push-Pull outputs to directly drive stepper idle air valve coils

settings.name: useRunningMathForCranking
settings.description: For cranking either use the specified fixed base fuel mass, or use the normal running math (VE table).

settings.name: useSeparateAdvanceForCranking
settings.description: In Constant mode, timing is automatically tapered to running as RPM increases. In Table mode, the "Cranking ignition advance" table is used directly.

settings.name: useSeparateAdvanceForIdle
settings.description: This activates a separate ignition timing table for idle conditions, this can help idle stability by using ignition retard and advance either side of the desired idle speed. Extra advance at low idle speeds will prevent stalling and extra retard at high idle speeds can help reduce engine power and slow the idle speed.

settings.name: useSeparateIdleTablesForCrankingTaper
settings.description: This uses separate ignition timing and VE tables not only for idle conditions, also during the postcranking-to-idle taper transition (See also afterCrankingIACtaperDuration).

settings.name: useSeparateVeForIdle
settings.description: This activates a separate fuel table for Idle, this allows fine tuning of the idle fuelling.

settings.name: useSpiImu
settings.description: If enabled - use onboard SPI Accelerometer, otherwise listen for CAN messages

settings.name: useStepperIdle
settings.description: This setting should only be used if you have a stepper motor idle valve and a stepper motor driver installed.

settings.name: useVssAsSecondWheelSpeed
settings.description: VSS and Aux Speed 1 or Aux Speed 1 with Aux Speed 2?

settings.name: valetModeRpmLimit
settings.description: Maximum RPM allowed when valet mode is active (CAN byte[4] of packet 0x181). Set to 0 to use normal hard limit.

settings.name: vbattDividerCoeff
settings.description: This is the ratio of the resistors for the battery voltage, measure the voltage at the battery and then adjust this number until the gauge matches the reading.

settings.name: verboseCan
settings.description: Print incoming and outgoing first bus CAN messages in evoTech console

settings.name: verboseCan2
settings.description: Print incoming and outgoing second bus CAN messages in evoTech console

settings.name: verboseIsoTp
settings.description: Are you a developer troubleshooting TS over CAN ISO/TP?

settings.name: verboseTriggerSynchDetails
settings.description: Verbose info in console below engineSnifferRpmThreshold

settings.name: verboseVVTDecoding
settings.description: Verbose info in console below engineSnifferRpmThreshold

settings.name: vfs.conditionsHoldTime
settings.description: Time that operating conditions must be stable before learning starts

settings.name: vfs.defaultEthanol
settings.description: [DEPRECATED] Now auto-derived from stoichRatioPrimary. Kept for config compatibility - not used by VFS.

settings.name: vfs.dfcoSettleTime
settings.description: Time after DFCO (fuel cut) before learning resumes

settings.name: vfs.enabled
settings.description: Enable Virtual Flex Fuel estimation when physical sensor is absent. Estimates ethanol content based on fuel trim (STFT + LTFT) corrections.

settings.name: vfs.gasolineCorrection
settings.description: Baseline fuel trim offset. Use this to compensate if your VE table has a systematic error. Set to 0 if VE table is well-tuned for your primary fuel.

settings.name: vfs.integratorSpeed
settings.description: Learning speed for ethanol estimation. Higher = faster learning but may oscillate. Lower = slower but more stable. 10 = very slow, 30 = default, 100 = fast

settings.name: vfs.maxLoad
settings.description: Maximum engine load for VFS estimation

settings.name: vfs.maxRpm
settings.description: Maximum RPM for VFS estimation

settings.name: vfs.minClt
settings.description: Minimum coolant temperature for VFS estimation to be active. Engine must be fully warmed up for accurate fuel trim readings.

settings.name: vfs.minLoad
settings.description: Minimum engine load for VFS estimation

settings.name: vfs.minRpm
settings.description: Minimum RPM for VFS estimation

settings.name: vfs.persistedEthanol
settings.description: Learned ethanol percent estimate, persisted across power cycles (docs/design/unified-learned-data-config.md). Not exposed as a dialog field - see vfsEstimatedEthanol for the live display value.

settings.name: vfs.timeoutSeconds
settings.description: Timeout before using last known value if conditions are not met

settings.name: vfs.transientSettleTime
settings.description: Time after acceleration/deceleration before learning resumes

settings.name: vssAccelThreshold
settings.description: Rate of change threshold for switching from steady-state to transient filtering.

settings.name: vssFilterReciprocal
settings.description: Set this so your vehicle speed signal is responsive, but not noisy. Larger value give smoother but slower response.

settings.name: vssGearRatio
settings.description: Number of turns of your vehicle speed sensor per turn of the wheels. For example if your sensor is on the transmission output, enter your axle/differential ratio. If you are using a hub-mounted sensor, enter a value of 1.0.

settings.name: vssMaxAccel
settings.description: Maximum plausible acceleration rate. Speed increases faster than this are rejected as noise.

settings.name: vssMaxAlpha
settings.description: Maximum EMA filter alpha for transients (1-100 = 0.01-1.0). Higher = faster response during acceleration/braking.

settings.name: vssMaxDecel
settings.description: Maximum plausible deceleration rate. Speed decreases faster than this are rejected as noise.

settings.name: vssMinAlpha
settings.description: Minimum EMA filter alpha for steady-state (1-100 = 0.01-1.0). Lower = stronger filtering, smoother but slower response.

settings.name: vssToothCount
settings.description: Number of pulses output per revolution of the shaft where your VSS is mounted. For example, GM applications of the T56 output 17 pulses per revolution of the transmission output shaft.

settings.name: vvlController.ignitionRetard
settings.description: Retard timing to remove from actual final timing (after all corrections) due to additional air.

settings.name: vvtActivationDelayMs
settings.description: We need to give engine time to build oil pressure without diverting it to VVT

settings.name: vvtControlMinClt
settings.description: Minimum coolant temperature to activate VVT

settings.name: warningPeriod
settings.description: set warningPeriod X

settings.name: wastegatePositionClosedVoltage
settings.description: Voltage when the wastegate is closed

settings.name: wastegatePositionOpenedVoltage
settings.description: Voltage when the wastegate is fully open

settings.name: widebandOnSecondBus
settings.description: Select which bus the wideband controller is attached to.

settings.name: wwaeAeFilmShare
settings.description: Share c of the acceleration enrichment (AE) that goes through the wall wetting film, from 0 to 1 (issue 36). 1.0 (factory default and what tunes saved before keep): the AE enters the film model with the base fuel, exactly the behavior before, so the film also amplifies the AE by 1/(1-beta). 0.0: the AE is added after the film, as an extra that is not amplified by it (the AE table already represents the fuel that wets the wall). In between: the film gets base + c*AE and the rest (1-c)*AE is added after it. Only matters with the wall wetting model on and the AE active.

settings.name: wwaeBeta
settings.description: 0 = No fuel settling on port walls 1 = All the fuel settling on port walls setting this to 0 disables the wall wetting enrichment.

settings.name: wwaeTau
settings.description: Length of time the deposited wall fuel takes to dissipate after the start of acceleration.
